title: New build apartment rental Bucharest: what you actually pay

description: New build apartment rental Bucharest: monthly costs, extra expenses, and when it is worth buying instead.

keywords: închiriere apartament bloc nou București, chirie bloc nou București, chirie apartament două camere, costuri închiriere apartament, garanție chirie, Titan Dristor
lead: Type new build apartment rental Bucharest into any search bar and you get hundreds of cloned listings: modern finishes, close to the subway, safe investment. Beneath these walls of text lies a market you can actually calculate: the Imospot guide from August 2026, based on 804 active offers, puts the median rent in Bucharest at around 600 euros per month. A new building pushes you above this average, and the real payment does not stop at the listing price. Below you can see where the rent for a new building starts, what drives it up, what you pay on top of it every month, how much it costs to move in, and when it is worth turning rent into a mortgage payment.

sections.h2: The real rent for a two-room apartment starts around 550 euros

blocks.x: The city average leads you down the wrong path because it lumps old neighborhood blocks together with brand new ones. If you look only at the new segment, a two-room apartment in a new building goes for 550 to 680 euros per month, according to NeoFort tracking from May 2026, compared to 550 euros for the same two rooms across the entire city on average. A studio sits at an average of 400 euros, and a three-room unit climbs to 799 euros. In Titan-Balta Alba, the area near Titan-Dristor, the median rent drops to 520 euros, and the median for Sector 3 as a whole is 500 euros, as shown by the Imospot guide published in August 2026.

sections.h2: Parking, furnishing, and the subway push your rent up

blocks.x: Listings for new buildings almost always come with the same three add-ons, each with its own price tag. King Imobiliare measured in July 2026 that a new building with a parking space raises your rent by 15 to 25% in the same area, while a fully furnished apartment rents for 15 to 20% more than an empty one and goes in days rather than weeks. The subway station works the same way: an apartment located 5 minutes from the station rents for 10 to 15% more than an identical one 20 minutes away on foot in the same neighborhood. If you aim high toward Sector 1, Floreasca, or Pipera, the parking space alone adds 50 to 80 euros per month, which explains why the median for Sector 1 sits at 825 euros, 65% above Sector 3.

sections.h2: In a new building with its own boiler, you control your winter bills

blocks.x: The difference between buildings shows up in January. The Imospot guide shows that in old buildings connected to the district heating system, the July bill compared to the January bill can differ by over 150 euros per month. A new building with underfloor heating and its own boiler works in reverse: you adjust consumption from the thermostat and pay for what you use, without the building district heating bill hanging over you.

Ilioara Residence, the building in Titan-Dristor that we use as a benchmark here, features a 24 kW Ariston boiler, underfloor heating in every room, and 7-chamber Tripan Salamander joinery, spread across a ground floor plus 8 stories. It is scheduled for completion in December 2026, so the first tenants will move into a fresh building with no consumption history. This standard is the benchmark you reach anyway when comparing new apartments in Bucharest before signing a rental agreement.

sections.h2: Moving into the apartment costs two to three times the monthly rent

blocks.x: The first day in a new apartment is not just a simple month of rent, as it represents the most expensive moment in a tenant year. RentnBuy calculated in February 2026 that the actual move-in cost is two to three times the monthly rent: for a two-room apartment at 800 euros per month through an agency, you shell out about 2,800 euros including the first month's rent, deposit, agency commission, and moving costs, whereas renting directly from the owner stops around 2,000 euros. After moving in, the monthly calculation climbs 20 to 30% above the displayed rent because maintenance, utilities, and parking spaces where applicable come into play.

sections.h2: Sign only after seeing the registered contract and the protocol with utility meter readings

blocks.x: The law requires the landlord to register the rental agreement with ANAF using form C168 within 30 days of signing. That registered contract serves as proof for your family doctor, kindergarten, and bank, so make sure to ask for a copy of the registration. At handover, the takeover protocol containing utility meter readings is the document that brings your deposit back when you leave, and the usual deposit amounts to one or two months of rent.

sections.h2: When it is worth turning rent into a mortgage payment

blocks.x: You pay rent anyway, month after month, and after five years you are left with paid rent and no apartment to show for it. Mortgage payments work in reverse, as the monthly payment eventually becomes your own apartment. The amount varies from person to person based on income and saved down payments, so we did not include specific mortgage figures here, but you can find the concrete steps from the first simulation to signing in the mortgage guide. As a comparison, a two-room apartment at Ilioara Residence starts at 107,500 euros excluding VAT, meaning around 130,075 euros once the 21% VAT is added, with a minimum down payment of 30%, equivalent to 32,250 euros. You buy the apartment directly from the developer with zero buyer commission, and apartment prices remain the place where you can check up-to-date figures.

faq.q: How much do you pay per month for two rooms in a new building?
faq.a: Between 550 and 680 euros, according to NeoFort data from May 2026. In the Titan-Balta Alba area, the median sits at 520 euros.

faq.q: What costs come on top of rent and how do you get your deposit back?
faq.a: The real monthly budget can rise by 20 to 30% above the displayed rent because winter maintenance and utilities come into play. In an old building on district heating, the January bill starts over 150 euros higher than the July one, while in a building with underfloor heating and its own boiler, you regulate consumption from the thermostat. Moving in through an agency requires about 2,800 euros for a two-room apartment renting at 800 euros per month, compared to roughly 2,000 euros directly from the owner. The usual deposit is one to two months of rent, and the handover protocol with utility meter readings is the document that gets it back to you upon departure.

faq.q: Is it worth switching from rent to a mortgage?
faq.a: When you have saved a down payment and rent payments add up year after year, the answer becomes yes. You pay rent anyway, whereas a mortgage leaves you with an apartment at the end. At Ilioara Residence, the minimum down payment for two rooms is 32,250 euros with zero buyer commission since you buy directly from the developer.
